Restrict a model to a region subset

Source: R/region.R
subset_model_regions.Rd

The spatial mirror of interpolating on a sampled calendar, usable up front: declares only region, drops trade routes that cross the subset boundary (with a message), and – when boundary_prices supplies a price for a dropped route – replaces it with an import/export stub at the kept endpoint. When the model carries a geoscale, it is filtered in step (recording coverage; see geoscales::geoscale_coverage()).

Usage

subset_model_regions(
  object,
  region,
  boundary_prices = NULL,
  verbose = isVerbose()
)

Arguments

object

a model.

region

character vector of regions to keep (must be a subset of the model's declared regions).

boundary_prices

optional data.frame pricing the boundary stubs of dropped routes, with columns src, dst, price, and optionally trade (object name; NA = any), year, timeslice (both NA = all), and cap.up (explicit stub bound overriding the derivation from the route's ava.* rows). Routes without a price row are dropped without a stub.

verbose

print per-object messages.

Value

the restricted model.

Details

The same behaviour is available without this verb by passing a geoscales::filter_geoscale() subset to interpolate_model().

See also

Other interpolation: interpolate_model(), with_solver_log()

Examples

repo <- newRepository(
  "mini",
  newCommodity("COA", unit = "MMBtu"),
  newCommodity("ELC", unit = "MWh", timeframe = "ANNUAL"),
  newSupply("SUP_COA", commodity = "COA", supply = data.frame(cost = 1)),
  newTechnology("ECOA", input = list(comm = "COA"), output = list(comm = "ELC"),
                cap2act = 1, invcost = list(invcost = 100),
                olife = list(olife = 30)),
  newDemand("DEM", commodity = "ELC",
            demand = data.frame(region = c("W1", "W2"), year = 2020, demand = 10))
)
mod <- newModel("MINI", data = repo, calendar = calendars$annual,
                region = c("W1", "W2"), horizon = horizons$Y2020_2060_by_5)

# keep one region; demand, capacity and routes outside it are dropped
sub <- subset_model_regions(mod, "W1")
get_region(sub)
#> [1] "W1"
